playbook.seek: Who to find: coaches, healers and guides who work in person in the region and already bring people together: life, health and wellness coaches, breathwork and meditation guides, somatic and bodywork practitioners, sound healers, retreat and ceremony leaders, doulas and nutrition coaches. Keep one only when a public page shows they host something for a group: a workshop, a circle, a group program, a retreat or a regular group session. Skip anyone who only works one to one.
playbook.signals: Strong signs, best first: a dated group offering in the next 60 days; a recurring circle or class with its own name; they teach at two or more local studios or rooms; their booking link goes to a general tool such as Calendly, Acuity or a ticket site, which means no home of their own; a newsletter sign-up or a line such as "join my community"; a named town or neighborhood on the page. Weak signs: a site that has not changed in a year, or no place name anywhere.
playbook.where: Where to look: the person's own website, single workshop or circle pages on Eventbrite, Meetup and Luma, the teachers and practitioners pages of studios and wellness centers, and local wellness directories.
playbook.queries: Searches that work: "<town> breathwork circle", "<town> women's circle", "<town> sound bath facilitator", "<town> life coach workshop", "<town> somatic workshop", "<town> meditation group", "<town> retreat leader", "<town> doula class", "<studio name> teachers". Use each area's own town names.
playbook.skip: Skip national coaching brands, online-only programs, anyone whose main offer is a certification or a course for other coaches, and medical or licensed therapy practices.
playbook.rank: Order leads.json best first, because only the first few are kept: a solo coach or guide with an upcoming group date and a listed email comes first, then one with a recurring group and a contact form, then the rest. One lead per person, even when they host several things.
playbook.record: In leads.json the event is the group thing they host: event.title is its name or what kind of thing it is, event.url is the public page that shows it, and starts_at may be empty. The organizer is the coach or guide.
playbook.note: Write a warm, human invite in four short paragraphs. 1: "Hi <first name>, your <practice or the thing they host, named loosely> caught my eye, and I love what you are up to." You may add one short, true line about it and one emoji that fits them; never give a date, time, price or place, and never describe a client, a result or a health claim. 2: "I'm Daniel, a local community builder and the founder of Frequency!" 3: "Frequency is a free way for neighbors to find or start local, in-person Circles and events around what they love. Right now I'm focused on the mindful, yogi and healer community, and on making it easy for hosts like you to make a big difference close to home." 4: one easy question that fits them, such as "Would you be interested in sharing your circle with neighbors nearby who are looking for one?", then "We're beta launching here in North County SD, and I would love for you to come check it out." Keep the quoted sentences as written. Use no exclamation mark besides the one in paragraph 2, and in a DM leave out the "Right now" sentence.
